title: Egress-weighting bug caused a 'Sibyl' regional stall and cross-tier misrouting — postmortem and corrective plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: On 2026-02-07 we observed a correlated drop in egress from a single region (eu-west-2) that our routing controller classified as 'degraded' and began draining. Due to a bug in the egress-weighting heuristics, the controller simultaneously over-assigned traffic to lower tiers and incompatible model variants, causing a cascading fallback surge and elevated error/latency rates for customer traffic. This ticket documents the timeline, root cause analysis, temporary mitigations, and the corrective roadmap to avoid recurrence.
detection_summary: First alert fired from the routing-traffic-imbalance dashboard (high outbound queue depth) at 2026-02-07T01:12Z. SRE paging triggered a severity-1 incident. Initial alerts were for increased 5xx rates in the eu-west-2 region and sustained high tail latency across the 'standard' tier. Automated canary health checks were noisy and did not prevent the routing controller from marking nodes as 'unhealthy' due to a thresholding bug in the egress-weighting calculation.
timeline: 2026-02-07T01:12Z - Grafana alert: eu-west-2 egress queue depth > 95th percentile. SRE S-Z paged.
2026-02-07T01:15Z - Traffic controller began rebalancing: reduced weight for eu-west-2, increased weight to lower-tier pools and fallback variants.
2026-02-07T01:18Z - Error rates increased on lower-tier pools; errors attributed to model variant incompatibility for some customer routes.
2026-02-07T01:25Z - Automated canary rollbacks attempted but mis-specified variant maps caused retries to escalate to further fallback variants.
2026-02-07T01:40Z - Emergency mitigation: turn off automatic rebalancing (manual gating) and enable per-route variant hard caps. Traffic stabilized over 12 minutes.
2026-02-07T02:10Z - Incident declared resolved for customer impact; retrospective analysis began.
2026-02-09 - Root cause review meeting with runtime, routing, and metrics teams.
2026-02-18 - Fix merged to correct egress-weighting smoothing window and add protective invariants (PR #8742).
2026-02-22 - Post-deploy verification completed; alert thresholds adjusted and runbook updated.
impact: Approximately 12 minutes of elevated errors and latencies affecting ~1.8% of overall production requests during the incident window. Several enterprise customers experienced degraded conversational latency and a small number (~30) saw malformed structured outputs due to mismatched model variants. No data exfiltration or security breach occurred.
root_cause: A logic error in the egress-weighting module combined two different smoothing techniques (rolling average and exponential decay) without reconciliation. When a short-lived spike in queue depth occurred, the controller over-interpreted the metric delta and applied a multiplicative weight reduction to the region. The weight adjustment code failed to enforce lower bounds and invariant checks, allowing the region weight to plummet to near-zero ('Sibyl stall'). The sudden weight shift triggered the multi-tier routing policy to spill traffic to lower-performance pools and incompatible model variants, which amplified errors and caused fallback loops.
contributing_factors: no invariant checks for minimum region weight
insufficient variant compatibility checks in the routing decision path
alerting thresholds were tuned for longer rolling windows and missed fast transient degradations
runbook did not include an automated circuit-breaker for aggressive rebalancing
immediate_mitigations: Disabled automatic global rebalancing for the affected cluster and moved to manual gating
Applied emergency per-route variant caps to prevent escalation into incompatible fallbacks
Scoped a temporary rate limit on lower-tier pools to reduce overload and backpressure
Reverted a recent tuning change to the canary health-check window made 24 hours earlier
long_term_fixes: Fix smoothing mismatch: unify to a single, well-documented EWMASmoothing class and add unit tests
Add invariant enforcement: never drop region weight below configurable floor (default 10%)
Variant compatibility matrix: static validation at deployment time and runtime checks to prevent routing to incompatible variants
Routing simulation harness: nightly job to run synthetic egress spikes through the controller and assert no >50% weight swing
Canary and alerting improvements: add short-window transient detectors and an 'abort rebalancing' automated circuit-breaker
Update runbook with explicit steps to disable automatic rebalancing and execute rapid hard caps
post_deploy_verification: After PR #8742 was merged and deployed, we ran 5 controlled spike simulations against eu-west-2 and observed max weight swing limited to 18% with no cross-tier spillover. Production metrics for 48 hours post-deploy show no recurrence. New alerts validated in staging and promoted to prod alerting groups.
follow_up_actions: ENG-82010 - Implement EWMASmoothing unit tests and integration tests (owner: runtime team, due 2026-03-10)
ENG-82011 - Add region weight floor and parameterize per-customer (owner: routing, due 2026-03-17)
ENG-82012 - Expand variant compatibility checks into the routing decision path (owner: model-onboarding, due 2026-03-24)
DOC-443 - Update Smart Routing runbook with Sibyl-stall section and post-incident checklist (owner: SRE-docs, due 2026-02-28)
OBS-91 - Create synthetic spike nightly job and dashboard to surface swings (owner: observability, due 2026-03-05)
Ops tabletop scheduled for Cycle 47 to validate runbook and simulation outputs
decisions: Roll back automatic global rebalancing while invariants and simulations are in place
Introduce a defensive lower bound (10%) for region weight, adjustable per deployment
Prioritize variant compatibility checks as a gate for routing changes
notes_and_lessons: Key lesson: aggressive automatic control loops that act faster than monitoring windows can compound transient failures into systemic ones. Routing decisions must be conservative by default, with explicit, testable invariants and a simulation harness that exercises fast transient paths. Observability must include both short-window detectors and long-window stability metrics.
final_status_comment: Fix deployed 2026-02-18 (PR #8742). Verified via synthetic spikes and 48-hour production observation window. Follow-up tickets created and owners assigned. Runbook updated and tabletop scheduled. Incident closed.
audit_trail: 2026-02-07T01:40Z - SRE disabled global rebalancer (manual action by Maya Chen)
